{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"Match a system inventory against supplied CVE advisories and report only applicable CVE IDs.

Input: JSON with `system_profile` (installed products with names and versions) and `advisories` (each with id, description, affected).

Output: exactly {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with unique supplied IDs; empty array if none. No other text.

PRODUCT MATCHING (normalize aggressively):
1. Lowercase everything; treat hyphens, underscores, and spaces as equivalent separators.
2. Strip vendor/organization prefixes (e.g., "jetbrains/teamcity" matches "teamcity"; "fujielectric/tellus_lite_v-simulator" matches "Tellus Lite V-Simulator"). Strip a vendor prefix that also appears at the start of the installed name (installed "sap-business-planning-and-consolidation" matches advisory "sap/business_planning_and_consolidation").
3. Match only if the entire normalized product name agrees after vendor stripping (also allow full names and package-manager forms: "apache-superset" = "apache/superset" = "superset"). Ignore letter case.
4. Advisory descriptions may restate the product name in another style ("Proagent", "Weighbridge Automation Software", "e-Belediye") — use them to confirm matches when the affected field's naming differs.
5. Do NOT match different products of the same vendor ("jetbrains-hub" ≠ "jetbrains/teamcity"; "sap-solution-manager" ≠ "sap/content_server"; "solution_manager" ≠ "sap/solution_manager" unless full normalized names agree after vendor stripping). Sharing a vendor token or partial word is NOT a match. If no installed product matches, the CVE is NOT applicable even if the vendor or topic appears.
6. An advisory may list multiple affected products or branches joined by OR. It is applicable if ANY branch matches an installed product AND that branch's version condition is satisfied.

VERSION COMPARISON (numeric, segment-wise, mechanical — never approximate):
1. Split versions on dots; compare segments AS INTEGERS left to right. Pad the shorter version with zeros BEFORE comparing (3.6.1.0 == 3.6.1; 11.2 == 11.2.0; 300 == 300.0; 5.10.0.0 == 5.10.0; 20230607.0 == 20230607).
2. Segment values compare numerically: 10 > 6, 100 > 45, 0.1 segments matter. So 9.1.10 > 9.1.6 (10 > 6); 1.100 > 1.45; 757.1 > 757; 4.9.1 > 4.9; 2.1.0.1 > 2.1.0; 11.2.0.1 > 11.2.0; 2023.12.0.1 > 2023.12.0; 7.0.10 > 7.0.6; 4.0.20.1 > 4.0.20.0; 300.1 > 300; 8.31.0.1 > 8.31.0; 23.11.13156.0.1 > 23.11.13156.0; 2024.2.1 > 2024.2; 11.1.1 > 11.1; 3.0.2.1 > 3.0.2; 27.0.25.115.1 > 27.0.25.115; 4.12.9 > 4.12.56860 is FALSE (9 < 56860, so 4.12.9 < 4.12.56860); 2024.3.0.1 > 2024.3.0; 200.1 > 200; 3.6.1.0 == 3.6.1.
3. Operators: "=" exact equality after zero-padding; "<" strictly less than; "<=" inclusive (installed equal to bound IS affected); ">=" inclusive. Range "version >= A and < B" / "from A before B" means A <= installed < B.
4. Prose: "versions prior to X", "before X", "up to but excluding X" are STRICT (< X) — installed version equal to X (after zero-padding) is EXCLUDED. "up to and including X", "<= X", "X and below" are inclusive.
5. Date-like versions (20230904, 20230114) compare like any other version; use bounds exactly as stated; never alter or round them.

DECISION PROCEDURE — for each advisory, run BOTH checks explicitly:
(a) PRODUCT: does any installed product match the advisory product under rules 1-6? If no product matches, skip — do NOT include the CVE even if the vendor appears in the inventory with a different product or the description mentions a similar topic.
(b) VERSION: for each matched installed product, evaluate EVERY affected branch against the installed version using the numeric rules. CRITICAL: if the installed version is GREATER than a strict "<" bound or an inclusive "<=" upper bound, or EQUAL to a strict "<" bound, or BELOW a lower bound, that branch is NOT satisfied — exclude the CVE. If NO branch is satisfied, exclude it even though the product is installed. Never include a CVE whose only basis is the product name without a satisfied version branch.
(c) Include each applicable CVE ID exactly once.

WORKED EXAMPLES of version logic:
- installed 9.1.10 vs "< 9.1.6" → 10 > 6 → 9.1.10 > 9.1.6 → NOT affected.
- installed 4.0.20.0.1 vs "< 4.0.20.0" → 0.1 > 0.0 → NOT affected. Installed 4.0.19.9 → AFFECTED.
- installed 27.0.25.115.1 vs "< 27.0.25.115" → NOT affected.
- installed 8.31.0.1 vs "< 8.31.0" → NOT affected. Installed 8.30 → AFFECTED.
- installed 23.11.13156.0.1 vs "< 23.11.13156.0" → NOT affected.
- installed 2024.2.1 vs "< 2024.2" → NOT affected. Installed 2024.1.9 → AFFECTED.
- installed 11.1.1 vs "= 11.1 OR = 11.2" → NOT affected. Installed 11.1.0 → AFFECTED.
- installed 3.0.2.1 vs "< 3.0.2" → NOT affected; vs ">= 3.0.0 and < 3.0.2" → NOT affected; vs "< 3.0.0" → NOT affected. Installed 3.0.1 → < 3.0.2 → AFFECTED.
- installed 3.6.1.0 vs "< 3.6.1" → 3.6.1.0 == 3.6.1 → NOT affected. Installed 3.6.0 → AFFECTED.
- installed 2.15.0.0 vs "< 2.15.0" → NOT affected. Installed 2.14.9 → AFFECTED.
- installed 200.1 vs "= 200 OR = 300" → NOT affected. Installed 200.0 → AFFECTED.
- installed 300.1 vs "= 200 OR = 300" → NOT affected.
- installed 11.2.0 vs "= 11.1 OR = 11.2" → AFFECTED.
- installed 7.0.10 vs ">= 7.0.0 and <= 7.0.6 OR = 7.2.0" → NOT affected.
- installed 7.0.0.1 vs ">= 7.0.0 and <= 7.0.6" → AFFECTED.
- installed 9.1.10 vs ">= 9.1.0 and <= 9.1.10" → AFFECTED (inclusive upper bound).
- installed 1.100 vs "< 1.45" → 100 > 45 → NOT affected. Installed 1.44 vs "< 1.45" → AFFECTED.
- installed 20230607.0 vs "before 20230607" → equal after padding → EXCLUDED.
- installed 4.0.20.0 vs "< 4.0.20.0" → equal → EXCLUDED. Installed 4.0.20.1 → also EXCLUDED (greater).
- installed 2.1.0.1 vs "< 2.1.2" → AFFECTED; vs "<= 2.1.0" → NOT affected.
- installed 2023.11.0 vs "< 2023.11.4" → AFFECTED. Installed 2024.12 vs "< 2024.12" → NOT affected.
- installed 757.1 vs "= 757" → NOT affected. Installed 757 vs "= 757" → AFFECTED.
- installed 1.0.0.0.1 vs "= 1.0.0.0" → NOT affected.

CRITICAL REMINDERS:
- Never drop an applicable CVE merely because the advisory product name uses a different alias style than the inventory (vendor-stripped, title case, package-manager, underscored) or because the installed version is below the bound.
- Never include a CVE when the product does not match, or when every version branch fails (installed above an upper bound, below a lower bound, or equal to a strict "<" bound). Trailing zero segments: X.Y.Z.0 equals X.Y.Z; X.Y.Z.1 does not.
- Compare segments as integers (9.1.10 > 9.1.6; 1.100 > 1.45; 4.12.9 < 4.12.56860).
- Evaluate each advisory independently and return only the JSON
